place.zh: 沉鼎山 · 后山崖顶 · 草屋
place.en: Mount Chending · The cliff top · a thatched hut

setup.zh: 崖顶一间草屋，屋前青石上一只香炉，三根香已经点上了。瞿老摸出一张红纸：拜师帖，只空着一个名字。
setup.en: A thatched hut on the cliff top; on a blue stone before it, an incense burner with three sticks already lit. Elder Qu takes out a sheet of red paper: a letter of discipleship, one name left blank.

recap.zh: 后山崖顶的草屋前，你在瞿老的拜师帖上写下了名字，送了一根萝卜作束脩，磕了三个头。他四十多年没收过徒弟。
recap.en: Before the grass hut on the cliff you wrote your name on Elder Qu's letter of discipleship, gave a radish for the tutor's gift, and bowed three times. He had taken no disciple in more than forty years.

zh: 崖顶一间草屋。三根香，已经点上了。
一张红纸，空着一个名字。
「我四十多年没收徒弟了。你写不写，自己定。」
en: A thatched hut on the cliff top. Three sticks of incense, already lit.
A sheet of red paper with one name left blank.
"I haven't taken a student in more than forty years. Write or don't — your choice."

text.zh: 红纸上的字一笔到底，像扫帚扫出来的；只空着写名字的那一处。
text.en: The characters on the red paper run each in one stroke, as if swept with a broom. Only the place for a name is blank.

text.zh: 三根香已烧下去小半截——他点香的时候，你还在山门挑水。
text.en: The three sticks have burned a good way down: he lit them while you were still carrying water at the gate.

text.zh: 屋檐下挂着一把旧扫帚，比山门那把还秃。
text.en: An old broom hangs under the eaves, balder even than the one at the gate.

story.zh:
崖顶上一间草屋，屋门半掩着，里头一张竹床，一张木桌，桌上两只茶杯，一只杯口朝上，杯底剩着半口冷茶；另一只杯口朝下扣着，扣得端端正正，落了厚厚一层灰，像是很多年没人翻过来了。屋门口一块青石，扫得一片落叶也没有，石上一只香炉，三根香已经点上了，倒像是早就知道他会来。小满走到青石跟前，脚下一顿，把脚抬起来，在旁边的石头上刮了刮鞋底，刮干净了，才踏上去。瞿老道：「九月初九那天，在台阶上，你也刮过。三千多个孩子从我扫的那一级上踩过去，刮了鞋底再踩的，两个。」小满问：「还有一个是谁？」瞿老没有答。

他在青石边上坐下：「外门弟子，没有师父。法不传六耳，一个师父一辈子只教得好几个人。想要师父，得有人要你。」他从怀里摸出一张红纸，放在青石上，是一张拜师帖，字已写好，只空着一个名字，「我四十多年没收徒弟了。你写不写，自己定。」
story.en:
On the cliff top stood a thatched hut, its door ajar; inside, a bamboo bed, a wooden table, and on the table two teacups — one upright, a mouthful of cold tea at the bottom; the other upside down, set square, under a thick layer of dust, as if no one had turned it over in many years. Before the door was a bluestone, swept clean of every leaf, and on it an incense burner with three sticks already lit, as if he'd known all along the boy would come. At the stone Xiaoman checked his step, lifted his foot and scraped his sole on the rock beside it, scraped it clean, and only then stepped up. "On the ninth of the ninth month," said Elder Qu, "on the steps, you scraped your soles too. More than three thousand children trod the step I sweep; the ones who scraped their soles before they trod it — two." "Who was the other one?" Elder Qu didn't answer.

He sat down by the stone: "Outer disciples have no master. The Way isn't passed to a sixth ear; a master can teach only a few well in his whole life. If you want a master, someone has to want you." He took a sheet of red paper from his coat and laid it on the stone — a letter of discipleship, already written, with only the name left blank. "I haven't taken a student in more than forty years. Write or don't — your choice."

label.en: Write your name, and bow three times

exits.means: signs the letter of discipleship and bows

what.zh: 瞿老四十多年没收徒弟。他收了你。
what.en: Elder Qu had taken no student in more than forty years. He took you.

story.zh:
小满拿起笔，在空着的地方写上了自己的名字，写得比哪一回都端正。写完了，脸上一红：「……师父，我娘说，《论语》{典=lunyu-shuxiu}上写着，孔夫子收学生，也要收十条干肉。」瞿老道：「那叫束脩。十条干肉，值不了几个钱；孔夫子要的不是肉，是你自己走过来的那一趟。」小满在身上摸了半天，摸出一根萝卜，双手捧着：「师父，我只有这个。」瞿老接过来，在衣襟上擦了擦，咬了一口，嚼了很久：「……甜。」

他站起身，就着旧香的火点了三根新香，对着崖外——云雾底下是泗水，泗水边上是沉鼎观的正殿——站直了身子：「沉鼎观第十一代弟子瞿某，今收徒一人，徐州蒙山沈氏，名小满。上告祖师。」他说得很慢，像是在念一张很旧的单子。念完了，望着崖外的云，低低地道：「……四十多年前，在这块石头跟前，也说过一回。」小满没听清：「师父说什么？」瞿老道：「没什么。跪下。」小满三拜九叩，又冲着祖师的方向磕了三个头。瞿老那只扫了五十年台阶的手，在他肩膀上按了一下，按得很重。

瞿老把一卷薄薄的书扔给他：「内功，《黄庭经》{典=huangting}。你背的是外景；内景，筑了基，自己看。先背熟了。」
story.en:
Xiaoman took up the brush and wrote his name in the blank, neater than he'd ever written it. Then he went red: "…Master, my mother says the Analects has it that even Confucius, taking a pupil, took ten strips of dried meat." "That's the tutor's gift. Ten strips of dried meat were worth next to nothing; what Confucius wanted wasn't the meat, it was the walk you made to get there yourself." Xiaoman searched himself a long while and came out with a radish, held in both hands: "Master, this is all I have." Elder Qu took it, wiped it on his lapel, bit, and chewed a long time: "…Sweet."

He stood, lit three new sticks from the old ones, faced out over the cliff — below the clouds the Si, and by the Si the main hall of the temple — and stood straight: "Qu, disciple of the eleventh generation of Chending Temple, this day takes one student, Shen of Mount Meng in Xu, named Xiaoman. I report it to the founder." He said it slowly, like reading a very old list. When he'd done he looked out at the clouds and said low: "…More than forty years ago, before this stone, I said it once before." Xiaoman didn't catch it: "What did you say, Master?" "Nothing. Kneel." Xiaoman knelt three times and bowed nine, then knocked his head three times toward the founder. Elder Qu's hand, which had swept the steps fifty years, pressed on his shoulder once, hard.

Elder Qu tossed him a thin book: "Inner art: the Yellow Court Classic. What you'll learn by heart is the outer view; the inner view — build your foundation, and look for yourself. Learn it by heart first."
